'''Hōri''' (祝) refers to individuals who serve deities in {{ill|Shinto|abstract|Q812767|af|Sjintoïsme|an|Xintoísmo|anp|शिन्तो धर्म|ar|شنتو|ary|شينطو|arz|شنتو|as|শ্বিণ্ট'|ast|Sintoísmu|az|Şintoizm|azb|شینتوئیسم|ba|Синтоизм|bat_smg|Šintoėzmos|bcl|Shinto|be|Сінтаізм|be_x_old|Сінтаізм|bg|Шинтоизъм|blk|ဆိဉ်တိုဘာႏသာႏ|bn|শিন্তৌ ধর্ম|bo|ཧྲིན་ཐོ།|br|Shintoegezh|bs|Šintoizam|bxr|Синто|ca|Xintoisme|ckb|شینتۆ|cs|Šintoismus|cy|Shintō|da|Shinto|de|Shintō|diq|Şinto|el|Σιντοϊσμός|eo|Ŝintoo|es|Sintoísmo|et|Šintoism|eu|Sintoismo|ext|Sintoísmu|fa|شینتو|fi|Šintolaisuus|fiu_vro|Sinto|fr|Shintoïsme|fur|Sintoisim|fy|Sjintoïsme|gcr|Shintoyism|gd|Shinto|gl|Xintoísmo|gn|Sinto|got|𐍃𐌹𐌽𐍄𐍉|gu|શિન્તો|ha|Shinto|he|שינטו|hi|शिन्तो धर्म|hif|Shinto|hr|Šintoizam|hu|Sintó|hy|Սինտոիզմ|ia|Shinto|id|Shinto|io|Shinto|is|Sjintóismi|it|Shintoismo|ja|神道|jam|Shinto|jv|Shinto|ka|შინტოიზმი|kbp|Sinto|kg|Kisinto|kk|Синтоизм|km|ស៊ិនតូ|kn|ಶಿಂಟೋ ಧರ್ಮ|ko|신토|ks|شِنتو|ky|Шинто|la|Sintoismus|lad|Shintoizmo|lb|Shintō|lfn|Xinto|lij|Scintoiximo|lt|Šintoizmas|lv|Sintoisms|map_bms|Shinto|mg|Sintôisma|min|Shinto|mk|Шинтоизам|ml|ഷിന്റൊ|mn|Шинто|mni|ꯁꯤꯟꯇꯣ ꯂꯥꯢꯅꯤꯡ|mr|शिंतो धर्म|ms|Shinto|mt|Xintù|mwl|Xintoísmo|my|ရှင်တိုဘာသာ|nds|Shintō|new|शिन्तो धर्म|nl|Shintoïsme|nn|Shinto|no|Shintōisme|oc|Sintoïsme|olo|Šintolaižus|or|କାମିନୋ ମିଚି|pa|ਸ਼ਿੰਤੋਵਾਦ|pl|Shintō|pms|Shintoism|pnb|شنتو|ps|شينتو|pt|Xintoísmo|ro|Șintoism|ru|Синтоизм|rue|Сінтоїзм|sc|Shintoismu|scn|Shintuismu|sco|Shinto|sd|شنٽو|sh|Šintoizam|simple|Shinto|sk|Šintoizmus|sl|Šintoizem|sn|Ushintho|so|Shiintismi|sq|Shinto|sr|Шинтоизам|sv|Shinto|sw|Shinto|ta|சிந்தோ|te|షింటో మతం|tg|Шинто|th|ชินโต|tl|Shinto|tly|Sintoizm|tok|nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto|tt|Щинто|tyv|Синтоизм|uk|Синто|ur|شنتو|uz|Sintoizm|vi|Thần đạo|war|Shinto|wuu|神道|xmf|სინტოიზმი|yi|שינטא|yo|Shinto|za|Saenzdaugyau|zgh|ⵜⴰⵛⵉⵏⵟⵓⵜ|zh|神道|zh_min_nan|Sîn-tō|zh_yue|神道|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto}}. It is a general term for those who offer their services to the gods, Ranking below {{ill|Kannushi|ja|神主|ko|신주|zh|神主|qid=Q15888735}} and {{ill|Negi|ja|禰宜|qid=Q11594490}} in the hierarchy. They are also known as '''Hōriko''' (祝子) and '''Hōribe''' (祝部).

== Overview ==
Hōri were among the ancient [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto priests]] who served at {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}} and were engaged in conducting {{ill|Festival|ar|مهرجان|arc|ܥܕܥܐܕܐ|as|উৎসৱ|ast|Festival|az|Festival|ba|Фестиваль|bcl|Festival|be|Фестываль|be_x_old|Фэстываль|bg|Фестивал|bn|উৎসব|bo|དུས་ཆེན།|br|Gouel-meur|bs|Festival|ca|Festival|chr|ᏓᎾᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ|ckb|فێستیڤاڵ|cs|Festival|csb|Festiwal|cy|Gŵyl|da|Festival|dag|Chuɣu|de|Festival|dga|Tigre|el|Πανηγύρι|eo|Festivalo|es|Festival|et|Festival|eu|Jaialdi|fa|جشنواره|fat|Afahyɛ|fi|Festivaali|fj|Yaloyalo|fr|Festival|fy|Festival|gl|Festival|gpe|Festival|he|פסטיבל|hi|उत्सव|hr|Festival|ht|Festival|hu|Fesztivál|hy|Փառատոն|id|Festival|is|Hátíð|it|Festival|ja|祭|kn|ಹಬ್ಬ|ko|축제|ku|Festîval|ky|Фестиваль|la|Festum|lt|Festivalis|lv|Festivāls|mai|पावनि|mk|Фестивал|ml|ഉത്സവം|mos|Kibsa|mr|उत्सव|ms|Festival|mzn|فسدوال|ne|चाडपर्व|new|नखः|nl|Festival|nn|Festival|no|Festival|pa|ਤਿਉਹਾਰ|pl|Festiwal|pnb|تہوار|pt|Festival|ro|Festival|ru|Фестиваль|rue|Фестівал|sa|भारतीयपर्वाणि|sd|ڏڻ|sh|Festival|simple|Festival|sk|Festival|sq|Festivali|sr|Фестивал|sv|Festival|ta|திருவிழா|tcy|ಪರ್ಬೊ|te|పండుగ|tg|Ҷашнвора|th|เทศกาล|tr|Festival|tw|Afahyɛ|uk|Фестиваль|ur|تہوار|uz|Festival|vi|Lễ hội|wuu|节日|yi|פעסטיוואל|zh|节日|zh_classical|節日|zh_yue|節|zu|Umkhosi|qid=Q132241}}. The earliest recorded Hōri is {{ill|Ōga no Higi|ja|大神比義|qid=Q119922506}}, who was appointed during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ar|الإمبراطور كيمي|arz|الامبراطور كيمى|azb|کیم‌می (ایمپیراتور)|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کینمێی|cs|Kinmei|de|Kimmei|es|Kinmei Tennō|fa|امپراتور کینمی|fi|Kinmei|fr|Kinmei|hr|Kinmei|id|Kaisar Kimmei|it|Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇|ka|კიმეი|ko|긴메이 천황|nl|Kimmei|pl|Kinmei|pt|Kimmei|ru|Император Киммэй|sh|Car Kimmei|simple|Emperor Kinmei|sl|Cesar Kinmei|sv|Kimmei|th|จักรพรรดิคิมเม|tl|Emperador Kimmei|tr|Kimmei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кіммей|uz|Imperator Kinmei|vi|Thiên hoàng Kimmei|yo|Emperor Kimmei|zh|钦明天皇|zh_min_nan|Kinmei Thian-hông|zh_yue|欽明天皇|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}} as the first priest of {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宇佐神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q715632}}, becoming its inaugural {{ill|Gūji|it|Gūji|ja|宮司|zh|宮司|qid=Q11453500}}.

Various etymologies are suggested for the term:
1. Derived from "Harafu" (to purify).
2. "Ha" meaning "feather," implying the movement of sleeves during sacred dances.
3. Related to "crawling in reverence" before the deities.

In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, it is recorded that {{ill|Iga-hiko|ja|伊賀彦|qid=Q140446104}} was appointed as a Hōri to enshrine the gods during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}. Additionally, mentions of Hōri serving at shrines in regions such as {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}} further confirm the early use of the title.

In different provinces:
- At {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} ({{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}), positions like ''Ōhōri'' and ''Gonhōri'' existed.
- At {{ill|Aso Shrine|en|Aso Shrine|qid=Q715639|lt=Aso Shrine}} ({{ill|Higo Province|en|Higo Province|qid=Q259705|lt=Higo Province}}), titles ranged from ''Ichihōri'' to ''Jūhōri'' (First to Tenth Hōri).
- Other notable shrines with historical Hōri roles include {{ill|Ōyamazumi Shrine|en|Ōyamazumi Shrine|qid=Q703904|lt=Ōyamazumi Shrine}}, {{ill|Kashima Jingū|en|Kashima Shrine|qid=Q706499|lt=Kashima Shrine}}, and {{ill|Kōra taisha|en|Kōra taisha|qid=Q715647|lt=Kōra Taisha}}.

In ancient times, Hōri were also called ''Hōribe''. The {{ill|Shokuinryō|ja|職員令|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q60996852}} mentions them, with descriptions in the {{ill|Ryō no Gige|ja|令義解}} explaining their selection and duties.

=== In Poetry ===
The {{ill|Man'yōshū|en|Man'yōshū|qid=Q834321|lt=Man'yōshū}} features a {{ill|sedōka|ja|旋頭歌|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q678489}} describing a sacred cedar tree worshiped by a Hōri of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|qid=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}:
{{Quotation|'''御幣取り 三輪の祝が 斎ふ杉原 薪伐り ほとほとしくに 手斧取らえぬ'''<br/>Translation: "Bearing sacred wands, the Hōri of Miwa reveres the sacred cedar grove; as he chops firewood, he nearly loses his axe."|Sedōka (Poem 1403)|''Man'yōshū'', Book VII}}

It also specifically refers to those Ranked below {{ill|Kannushi|ja|神主|ko|신주|zh|神主|qid=Q15888735}} and {{ill|Negi|ja|禰宜|qid=Q11594490}} in service to the gods. It is also known as '''Hōriko''' (祝子) or '''Hōribe''' (祝部).

The earliest historical mention of Hōri dates to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ar|الإمبراطور كيمي|arz|الامبراطور كيمى|azb|کیم‌می (ایمپیراتور)|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کینمێی|cs|Kinmei|de|Kimmei|es|Kinmei Tennō|fa|امپراتور کینمی|fi|Kinmei|fr|Kinmei|hr|Kinmei|id|Kaisar Kimmei|it|Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇|ka|კიმეი|ko|긴메이 천황|nl|Kimmei|pl|Kinmei|pt|Kimmei|ru|Император Киммэй|sh|Car Kimmei|simple|Emperor Kinmei|sl|Cesar Kinmei|sv|Kimmei|th|จักรพรรดิคิมเม|tl|Emperador Kimmei|tr|Kimmei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кіммей|uz|Imperator Kinmei|vi|Thiên hoàng Kimmei|yo|Emperor Kimmei|zh|钦明天皇|zh_min_nan|Kinmei Thian-hông|zh_yue|欽明天皇|qid=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei}}, when {{ill|Ōga no Higi|ja|大神比義|qid=Q119922506}} was appointed Japan's first Hōri and became the initial {{ill|Gūji|it|Gūji|ja|宮司|zh|宮司|qid=Q11453500}} of {{ill|Usa Jingū|ja|宇佐八幡宮|lt=Usa Hachiman-gū}}.<ref>Ogawa Shin'ichi, *Usa Jingū to Ōgami-shi*, Bungeisha.</ref><ref>Kokugakuin University Japanese Culture Research Institute, *Shinto Jiten*.</ref><ref>Nakano Hatanosu, *Hachiman Shinkō*, p. 91.</ref><ref>*Kami Iwa Shimizu Monjo*, Hōki 4 (774).</ref><ref>*Ōgami-shi Kaden*.</ref><ref>*Kōnin Kanpu* (cited in *Kōnin Roku*, 815).</ref>

The etymology of "Hōri" has been the subject of various theories:
1. Derived from the term "hara(u)" (to cleanse).
2. Related to "ha" (羽, feather), as it is said that performers waved their sleeves in ritual dances.
3. Originating from the verb "haifu" (匍匐在), meaning "to crawl humbly in service to the gods."

The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}, {{ill|Iga Hiko|ja|伊賀彦|qid=Q140446104}} was appointed Hōri to enshrine the gods. Later references in the same chronicle during the reign of {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} mention Hōri serving at shrines in {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}, such as the {{ill|Otakesha Shrine|ja|小竹社|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579151}} and Amanosha Shrine.

Notable examples of Hōri across Japan include:
- In {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} ({{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, present-day Nagano Prefecture), titles such as {{ill|Hōri|ja|大祝|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祝 (神職)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24869239}} and Gonhōri (権祝) existed in the early {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}.
- In {{ill|Aso Shrine|en|Aso Shrine|qid=Q715639|lt=Aso Shrine}} ({{ill|Higo Province|en|Higo Province|qid=Q259705|lt=Higo Province}}, present-day Kumamoto Prefecture), there were titles such as Ichihōri through Jūhōri (One through Ten Hōri), as well as Kuni no Miyatsuko Hōri and Kanekoboru Hōri.
- In {{ill|Ōyamazumi Shrine|en|Ōyamazumi Shrine|qid=Q703904|lt=Ōyamazumi Shrine}} ({{ill|Iyo Province|en|Iyo Province|qid=Q907829|lt=Iyo Province}}, present-day Ehime Prefecture), an Ōhōri served a central role.
- Other examples include the ancient Hōri roles at {{ill|Kashima Jingū|en|Kashima Shrine|qid=Q706499|lt=Kashima Shrine}} ({{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353|lt=Hitachi Province}}) and {{ill|Kōra taisha|en|Kōra taisha|qid=Q715647|lt=Kōra Taisha}} ({{ill|Chikugo Province|en|Chikugo Province|qid=Q864159|lt=Chikugo Province}}).

Historically, Hōri were also referred to as Hōribe (祝部). The {{ill|Ritsuryō|ja|律令制度|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 律令制|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q742460}} codified their roles in the {{ill|Shokuinryō|ja|職員令}}, which stated that:
> "The Hōribe (meaning those who act as ritual leaders) shall be selected by provincial governors from among the {{ill|Kobe|ja|神戸|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11589706}} (shrines’ hereditary communities). If no suitable candidates exist within the Kambe, individuals may be chosen from the general populace."<ref>*Shokuinryō*.</ref>
